course_metadata.course_description: An in-depth study of fundamental data structures and algorithms, including arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, sorting, searching, recursion, dynamic programming, and algorithmic complexity. Prerequisite: CS101.

course_outcomes.description: Identify the operations supported by a binary search tree.
Define the difference between contiguous and linked memory.
Analyze the time complexity of quicksort in the worst case.
Demonstrate the use of dynamic programming to solve a problem.
Exhibit respect for ethical considerations in algorithm design.

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain the core concepts, terminology, and purpose of Introduction to Data Structures.
Apply the principles of Introduction to Data Structures to solve a small, worked example in a lab setting.
Collaborate with peers to review, critique, and improve an implementation of Introduction to Data Structures.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Introduction to Data Structures + Hands-on Lab in VS Code: applying Introduction to Data Structures to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the difference between stack and queue data structures in C++17 and describe their primary operations (push, pop for stack; enqueue, dequeue for queue).
Apply the concept of stacks and queues to solve a problem involving managing function calls in a C++17 program, such as using std::function and std::stack.
Collaborate in a hands-on lab using GDB to debug and test the implementation of stacks and queues in a C++17 project, ensuring the correct order of operations and edge cases are handled.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Stacks and Queues + Hands-on Lab in PyCharm: applying Stacks and Queues to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the difference between a binary tree and a binary search tree in PostgreSQL 16 and explain their properties.
Implement a breadth-first search (BFS) algorithm in Python 3.12 to traverse a tree structure in a Jupyter Notebook.
Collaborate with a partner to debug and correct a DFS implementation in C++17 using GDB in a PostgreSQL 16 environment.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Trees and Graphs + Hands-on Lab in C++17 with GDB: applying Trees and Graphs to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the time complexity of QuickSort and why it is considered efficient for certain data sizes.
Apply the partitioning step of QuickSort algorithm in a hands-on CMake lab using Google Test.
Collaborate in debugging a QuickSort implementation that exhibits stack overflow issues using GDB.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Sorting Algorithms + Hands-on Lab in Python 3.12: applying Sorting Algorithms to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the time complexity of binary search and explain why it is O(log n) using C++17 and std::vector.
Apply the concept of binary search to solve a problem of finding an element in a sorted array using Python 3.12 and std::vector.
Collaborate in a Git lab to integrate binary search implementation into a larger project, ensuring code quality and maintainability.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Searching Algorithms + Hands-on Lab in Jupyter Notebook: applying Searching Algorithms to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the base case and recursive case in a recursive function using C++17 and Debug with GDB in Valgrind.
Apply tail recursion optimization principles to improve the efficiency of a recursive function in Python 3.12 and test with pytest.
Collaborate in designing a recursive algorithm for a complex problem and implement it in C++17, debugging with GDB in Valgrind.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Recursion + Hands-on Lab in CMake with Google Test: applying Recursion to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the key characteristics of the Knapsack problem and explain how they differ from other combinatorial optimization problems.
Apply the concept of memoization to design an efficient algorithm for solving the 0/1 Knapsack problem using Python 3.12.
Collaborate with a team to integrate the implemented Knapsack algorithm into a larger project using PyCharm and Git for version control.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Dynamic Programming + Hands-on Lab in PostgreSQL 16: applying Dynamic Programming to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the Big O notation for sorting algorithms and explain why it's important for algorithmic complexity.
Apply the concept of time complexity in analyzing the performance of a recursive algorithm implemented in C++17.
Collaborate in a scenario where you analyze the algorithmic complexity of a database query optimization in PostgreSQL 16 using CMake.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Algorithmic Complexity + Hands-on Lab in Git: applying Algorithmic Complexity to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the key topics covered in the Midterm Assessment and Review session using GDB for debugging Python 3.12 code.
Apply the principles of exception handling in Python 3.12 to solve a problem during the hands-on lab in PyCharm.
Collaborate with peers in a PyCharm environment to debug and optimize a mid-sized Python 3.12 project.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Midterm Assessment and Review + Hands-on Lab in Valgrind: applying Midterm Assessment and Review to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the difference between breadth-first search (BFS) and depth-first search (DFS) traversal algorithms in a graph using GDB to debug a DFS implementation.
Apply Dijkstra's algorithm to find the shortest path in a weighted graph using PyCharm to implement the algorithm in Python 3.12.
Collaborate with a peer to debug and optimize a breadth-first search implementation in C++17 using Visual Studio Code (VS Code) for code review.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Graph Traversal Algorithms + Hands-on Lab in Catch2: applying Graph Traversal Algorithms to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the difference between Dijkstra's algorithm and Bellman-Ford algorithm for solving the single-source shortest path problem in a graph.
Apply Dijkstra's algorithm in a Jupyter Notebook using Python 3.12 and PostgreSQL 16 to find the shortest path in a weighted graph scenario.
Collaborate with a peer to debug a segmentation fault encountered during the implementation of Dijkstra's algorithm in C++17 using std::vector.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Shortest Path Algorithms + Hands-on Lab in VS Code: applying Shortest Path Algorithms to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the difference between Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms for constructing a Minimum Spanning Tree.
Apply Kruskal's algorithm to solve a Minimum Spanning Tree problem using a weighted graph in C++17 with std::vector and std::set.
Collaborate with a peer to debug and optimize a Minimum Spanning Tree implementation in CMake using Google Test for testing.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Minimum Spanning Trees + Hands-on Lab in PyCharm: applying Minimum Spanning Trees to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the role of hash functions in the construction of hash tables and explain their properties.
Apply the principles of chaining and open addressing to resolve collisions in hash tables.
Demonstrate the use of Git for version control while implementing a hash table data structure in C++17.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Hash Tables and Hashing + Hands-on Lab in C++17 with GDB: applying Hash Tables and Hashing to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the properties of an AVL tree and how they ensure balance during insertions and deletions.
Apply AVL rotations to rebalance a tree after insertion of a node with a key that causes an imbalance.
Collaborate with a peer to debug a recursive AVL tree insertion function using GDB in a C++17 environment.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Balanced Trees (AVL, Red-Black) + Hands-on Lab in Python 3.12: applying Balanced Trees (AVL, Red-Black) to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain the core concepts, terminology, and purpose of Greedy Algorithms.
Apply the principles of Greedy Algorithms to solve a small, worked example in a lab setting.
Collaborate with peers to review, critique, and improve an implementation of Greedy Algorithms.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Greedy Algorithms + Hands-on Lab in Jupyter Notebook: applying Greedy Algorithms to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the role of backtracking in solving the Eight Queens problem and how it differs from the brute-force approach.
Apply the branch-and-bound algorithm to solve the Knapsack problem with a given set of items and weights.
Collaborate in a hands-on lab using GDB to analyze the efficiency of your implemented backtracking and branch-and-bound algorithms.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Backtracking and Branch-and-Bound + Hands-on Lab in CMake with Google Test: applying Backtracking and Branch-and-Bound to a worked problem

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the key components and requirements for a successful capstone project using Python 3.12 and PyCharm.
Apply best practices for setting up a project environment in PyCharm, including version control with Git and dependency management with CMake.
Construct a detailed project plan that includes milestones, deliverables, and ethical considerations, using a project management tool like Jira.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Capstone Project Preparation + Hands-on Lab in PostgreSQL 16: applying Capstone Project Preparation to a worked problem

weekly_schedule.topic: Final Project Defense and Comprehensive Review

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify the key components of a successful Final Project Defense presentation and explain their importance using Python 3.12.
Apply best practices for code review in Python 3.12 during the Final Project Comprehensive Review session.
Collaborate with peers to provide constructive feedback on the Final Project using a Jupyter Notebook for documentation and analysis.

weekly_schedule.teaching_activities: Face-to-face lecture on Final Project Defense and Comprehensive Review + Hands-on Lab in Git: applying Final Project Defense and Comprehensive Review to a worked problem
